_comment:
'Whenever Hornet's Sting defends, reveal the top card of your deck. If it's an arrow, deal 1 damage to the attacking hero or ally. Otherwise, put it on the bottom of your deck.' Ranger Equipment - Arms (Dynasty) + printed **Blade Break**.

BLADE BREAK NOT AUTHORED: it appears in printed_keywords, so it fires from the card DB keywords field engine-side; re-authoring it would be a defect.

TRIGGER: TRIGGERED ON_DEFEND - shape copied from SHIPPED ast/zap_clappers.json, which pairs the same defend trigger with a reveal and damage to the attacker ('the ATTACKING hero' from a WHEN-THIS-DEFENDS trigger is the exact case _damage_target_player documents ATTACKER for).

REVEAL: REVEAL_TOP_DECK reads amount and into (effect_types.py:2229-2256); with into:'revealed' it stores the revealed card(s) as a list under that ref without moving them.

BRANCH: CONDITIONAL with when/then/else (effect_types.py:3697-3724) - deliberately NOT 'conditions', which the loader pops as an effect-level gate and would skip the whole branch including the else. The when-test REF_IS_TYPE (condition_types.py:2011-2043) takes ref+types and unions TYPES AND SUBTYPES, so ['Arrow'] matches Arrow-the-subtype; it also handles a one-element list correctly (takes the single entry), which matters because REVEAL_TOP_DECK always stores a list. If arrow: DEAL_GENERIC amount 1 target ATTACKER - _damage_target_player (effect_types.py:907-931) resolves ATTACKER to combat.attacker_id, i.e. the opposing hero, exactly the defender-sourced case zap_clappers ships. Otherwise: PUT_REF_BOTTOM ref 'revealed' (effect_types.py:3614-3639), whose default player OWNER routes to the card's owner's deck bottom - here the controller's own deck, which is whose deck was revealed. If the revealed card IS an arrow it stays where it is (top of deck): the printed text only moves it in the otherwise case.

GAP - CLAUSE 'deal 1 damage to the attacking hero OR ALLY': DEAL_GENERIC damages a PLAYER; its target vocabulary resolves ATTACKER to combat.attacker_id (a player id), so when the attack came from an ALLY the printed text wants the damage on the ally OBJECT, and no DEAL_* target string names an attacking ally. Drafted as damage to the attacking player (hero), which is right whenever a hero attacked and over-applies only vs ally attacks. A fix needs a DEAL target that resolves to the current attack's source object.

Release note ('if the damage kills an attacking Ally, the combat chain closes before the reaction step') is engine state-based-action behaviour around ally death - nothing to author in JSON.
